collection.description: Young villagers ask why different communities have distinct languages, traditions, and histories.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Young villagers ask why different communities have distinct languages, traditions, and histories.

choices.label: Compare Objects Made in Different Places
Ask Whether Differences Make People Unequal

a1.name: Outcome A1
a1.text: They learn that communities develop through movement, contact, and time.

a2.name: Outcome A2
a2.text: (child) notices that traditions can be shared without becoming identical.

b1.name: Outcome B1
b1.text: Stories reveal both connections and disagreements.

b2.name: Outcome B2
b2.text: Some families have forgotten parts of their histories, and no one invents certainty.

c1.name: Outcome C1
c1.text: The children admire multiple ways to solve the same practical problem.

c2.name: Outcome C2
c2.text: They discover that similar objects can carry very different meanings.

d1.name: Outcome D1
d1.text: The adults firmly reject that conclusion without denying real differences.

d2.name: Outcome D2
d2.text: (child) recognizes that fairness does not require everyone to be the same.
